action: Restart Payment API Kubernetes deployment
result: Timeouts stopped for about 20 minutes, then returned as the connection pool filled again.

action: Increase API timeout from 3s to 8s
result: Requests waited longer and still timed out. Database connection wait time remained high.

action: Increase database connection pool maximum from 20 to 100
result: Connection wait time dropped and intermittent payment timeouts stopped under peak traffic.

action: Restart Payment API container
result: Latency dipped briefly, then tracked the same elevated provider response times.

action: Increase payment authorisation timeout
result: A subset of checkouts completed, but provider-side slowness continued and many requests still timed out.

action: Inspect external payment provider status page and latency probes
result: Confirmed regional degradation on fictional-pay while MongoDB connection utilisation stayed healthy.

action: Activate fallback provider routing to fictional-pay-backup
result: Checkout latency returned to baseline on the backup provider path.

action: Restart Payment API pods
result: Pods came back healthy but continued returning provider authentication failures.

action: Inspect database health and connection pool metrics
result: Database metrics were normal. No evidence of pool saturation or query regressions.

action: Verify fictional-pay API credentials against the provider console
result: Identified that credential fp-key-2025-q3 had expired on 2026-02-01.

action: Rotate external payment-provider secret and update credentialId
result: Provider accepted the new key and immediate 401/403 payment rejections stopped.

action: Restart Payment API Kubernetes deployment
result: Accepted payments continued, but the processing backlog only shrank briefly before growing again.

action: Scale API replicas without changing worker capacity
result: Ingress capacity improved, yet settlement delay stayed high because workers remained saturated.

action: Inspect payment-processing queue depth and worker lag
result: Queue depth was climbing while only two workers were active.

action: Increase payment worker replicas from 2 to 6
result: Backlog drained and delayed settlements returned to normal.

action: Restart Authentication Service pods
result: Login improved for several minutes, then session lookup timeouts returned.

action: Increase token TTL to reduce session reads
result: Session store connection wait time stayed elevated. TTL was not the bottleneck.

action: Increase Redis connection pool maximum from 10 to 50
result: Session lookup latency returned to baseline and intermittent auth failures stopped.

action: Restart Authentication Service deployment
result: New pods loaded the same expired signing certificate and continued rejecting tokens.

action: Inspect JWT signing certificate expiry and key id
result: Certificate auth-signing-2025-z had expired on 2026-04-10.

action: Rotate signing credentials to auth-signing-2026-b
result: Token validation succeeded and users could authenticate again.

action: Restart canary Authentication Service pods
result: Canary pods restarted with the same incorrect AUTH_SESSION_URL and kept failing.

action: Compare canary and stable environment variables
result: Found AUTH_SESSION_URL pointing at redis-sessions-v3-wrong-host on the canary only.

action: Rollback canary deployment and restore session-store endpoint
result: Authentication error rate returned to normal on all traffic.

action: Restart notification workers
result: Queue depth dipped slightly, then climbed again.

action: Increase worker concurrency without changing prefetch
result: Workers stayed underutilised because prefetch remained set to 1.

action: Restore worker concurrency to 8 and prefetch to 20
result: Notification backlog drained and delivery delay returned to normal.

action: Retry failed notification batches immediately
result: Retries amplified HTTP 429 responses from fictional-mail.

action: Inspect provider response codes and retry histograms
result: Confirmed sustained rate limiting at the previous 1200 sends/minute target.

action: Lower maxSendRatePerMinute to 600 and enable provider-aware backoff
result: 429 responses stopped and delivery recovered without growing the retry storm.
